$comment: Trusted text read as the markup it writes, judged by both editors alike: a literal Trusted value, or a val set to one, is read in place in a call to interpolate and in a Kotlin template, so the values after it are judged where they really land; a Trusted whose text is not known leaves what follows it at most a warning, and the literal Trusted itself is the author's own markup.

cases.name: a literal Trusted attribute name puts the value in a Datastar expression
cases.source:
import io.github.markusaugust.streamlord.core.domain.*
fun f(q: String) = interpolate("<button %s=\"%s\">Go</button>", Trusted("data-on:click"), q)

issues.message: interpolate always throws here: q lands in data-on:click, which Datastar runs as an expression or follows as a signal path, and only a number or a boolean is let in there. Put the value in a signal and reference it from the expression, or write the signal's name in the markup yourself.

cases.name: a literal Trusted attribute name before a number is let in
cases.source:
import io.github.markusaugust.streamlord.core.domain.*
fun f(n: Int) = interpolate("<button %s=\"%s\">Go</button>", Trusted("data-on:click"), n)

cases.name: a literal Trusted tag name puts the value in code
cases.source:
import io.github.markusaugust.streamlord.core.domain.*
fun f(q: String) = interpolate("<%s>%s</%s>", Trusted("script"), q, Trusted("script"))

issues.message: interpolate always throws here: q lands in a script or style element, which the browser runs, and only Trusted(...) is let in there. Put the value in a data-* attribute or a signal and read it from there; wrap markup you built yourself in Trusted(...).

cases.name: a literal Trusted href is a URL, escaped and checked as interpolate checks one
cases.source: import io.github.markusaugust.streamlord.core.domain.* fun f(q: String) = interpolate("x", Trusted("href"), q)

cases.name: a literal Trusted src of a script loads code from wherever the value points
cases.source:
import io.github.markusaugust.streamlord.core.domain.*
fun f(q: String) = interpolate("<script %s=\"%s\"></script>", Trusted("src"), q)

issues.message: interpolate always throws here: q lands in src, which loads code from wherever the value points, and the markup before it does not fix the host. Only Trusted(...) is let in there. Start the value with a path such as /js/ or a whole origin such as https://cdn.example/, so that the value only picks a file there, or wrap a URL you chose yourself in Trusted(...).

import io.github.markusaugust.streamlord.core.domain.*
fun f(q: String) = interpolate("<%s src=\"%s\"></%s>", Trusted("script"), q, Trusted("script"))

issues.message: interpolate always throws here: q lands in src, which loads code from wherever the value points, and the markup before it does not fix the host. Only Trusted(...) is let in there. Start the value with a path such as /js/ or a whole origin such as https://cdn.example/, so that the value only picks a file there, or wrap a URL you chose yourself in Trusted(...).

import io.github.markusaugust.streamlord.core.domain.*
fun f(q: String) = interpolate("<%s src=\"/js/%s\"></%s>", Trusted("script"), q, Trusted("script"))

cases.name: a Trusted whose text is not known makes what follows it uncertain
cases.source:
import io.github.markusaugust.streamlord.core.domain.*
fun f(a: String, q: String) = interpolate("<button %s data-on:click=\"%s\">Go</button>", Trusted(a), q)

issues.message: interpolate throws here unless the Trusted text before q moves it: it lands in data-on:click, which Datastar runs as an expression or follows as a signal path, where only a number or a boolean is let in. Put the value in a signal and reference it from the expression, or write the signal's name in the markup yourself.

cases.name: a const val named in a Trusted is not known text and stays silent
cases.source:
import io.github.markusaugust.streamlord.core.domain.*
const val TAG = "section"
fun f(q: String) = interpolate("<%s class=\"lt-card\">%s</%s>", Trusted(TAG), q, Trusted(TAG))

cases.name: a literal Trusted attribute name in a Kotlin template puts the value in a Datastar expression

issues.message: Kotlin interpolates $q here, as the whole Datastar expression. Meant as a server value, only a number or a boolean is safe there; meant as the signal $q, make the whole literal $$"""...""" (Kotlin 2.2+), or escape as ${'$'}q.
fixes:
fun f(q: String) = $$"<button $${Trusted("data-on:click")}=\"$q\">Go</button>"
fun f(q: String) = "<button ${Trusted("data-on:click")}=\"${'$'}q\">Go</button>"
fun f(q: String) = "<button ${Trusted("data-on:click")}=\"\$q\">Go</button>"

cases.name: a literal Trusted tag name in a Kotlin template puts the value in code

issues.message: Kotlin writes $q into a script or style element, which the browser runs, so escaping does not help. Put the value in a data-* attribute or a signal and read it from there.

cases.name: a literal Trusted path in a Kotlin template fixes the host of a URL that loads code

issues.message: Kotlin writes $q into the HTML as it is. If it can hold text from outside, build the string with interpolate(...), which escapes it.
fixes:
import io.github.markusaugust.streamlord.core.domain.interpolate

fun f(q: String) = interpolate("<script src=\"%s%s\"></script>", Trusted("/js/"), q).text

cases.name: a literal Trusted src in a Kotlin template loads code from wherever the value points

issues.message: Kotlin writes $q into src, which loads code from wherever the value points, and the markup before it does not fix the host: even an https:// URL can load code from another origin. Escaping does not help. Start the value with a path such as /js/ or a whole origin such as https://cdn.example/, so that the value only picks a file there.
